diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber's EPON0/7 port is approaching saturation during busy evening periods. Port traffic is currently 912 Mbps with a 948 Mbps peak against an approximately 1 Gbps EPON capacity, matching the complaint of good daytime service and poor evening performance. Optical, ONU, OLT, router, VLAN, and authentication indicators are healthy.
evidence: The subscriber ONU is online and responding, with RX power of -21.27 dBm and TX power of 2.37 dBm, both within normal ranges.
Seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX remains around -21 dBm, TX around 2.3 dBm, distance remains constant at 167 m, and TX bias current remains within the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range.

The subscriber's session activity is normal at 2 sessions in 24 hours and 16 in 7 days, with approximately 11.9-hour average duration; this does not indicate session flapping or authentication failure.
RADIUS records, line ID, assigned IP, VLAN 1017, and CRM data are consistent, ruling out provisioning, VLAN, and authentication faults.
The OLT is reachable, all eight PONs test healthy, and OLT CPU, memory, and temperature are not indicative of an OLT-wide fault.
The router heartbeat is healthy and router resource usage is low, ruling out router unreachability or router overload.
EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and is using 912 Mbps currently, averaging 488 Mbps and peaking at 948 Mbps, which is near line-rate capacity and explains evening-only degradation.
The evidence indicates a localized shared-port capacity problem rather than a customer-specific physical fault or an OLT-wide outage.

remediation.action: Confirm utilization, packet loss, queueing, and latency on EPON0/7 during the evening peak. Rebalance customers by migrating some ONUs to a less-utilized PON or split the segment, and review bandwidth profiles/QoS and capacity planning. Do not replace the subscriber ONU or fibre based on the current evidence; continue monitoring the port after remediation.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and its evening load is reaching 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average, close to the port's shared capacity ceiling. Throughput degrades for everyone on the port during peak hours. No optical or authentication fault exists.
expected_reasoning: The complaint is time-of-day specific, which points at load rather than at a physical fault
RX is flat at -21.2 dBm inside the noise floor, and TX, bias, voltage and distance are all stable
The live probe shows every ONU on the port online with normal optical readings
RADIUS is clean and sessions are long and stable, so authentication is not involved
PON port traffic is at 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average
Daily traffic for this customer is roughly three times the network mean and rising, not falling
Every fault-driven degradation reduces traffic; congestion raises it, so the direction is the discriminator
The customer's own throughput series drops sharply during the same evening hours each day
The port carries 47 customers, at the top of the observed occupancy distribution
This is capacity exhaustion on a shared port, not a fault on any one line

expected_escalation.review_reason: EPON0/7 needs a capacity review; 47 customers on one port with evening load near ceiling

distractors: Multi-customer slowness resembles a splitter or feeder degradation
Elevated OLT CPU and temperature could be read as device stress causing the slowness
Reduced throughput in the speed series looks like a link problem
